faqs.a: On a pure black slide, a dead pixel stays black (invisible), so check the white and colored slides: a dead pixel appears as a permanent tiny black dot on every slide, while a stuck pixel glows one color (red, green, or blue) constantly. Mark the spot and zoom in with your phone camera to confirm.
faqs.q: How do I spot a dead pixel?

faqs.a: Yes — run the refresh-rate measurement while plugged in and with nothing else running. Browsers cap rendering at the display's refresh rate, so the result reflects your panel. On 120 Hz phones the measurement should read near 120 Hz.
faqs.q: Can I test my phone's 120 Hz screen?

faqs.a: Slight bleed on IPS panels is common and usually harmless. Strong yellowish patches in the corners on the black slide, visible during normal dark scenes, are worth a warranty claim. Take a photo of the black slide as evidence.
faqs.q: What is backlight bleed and should I worry?

faqs.a: Banding — visible steps instead of a smooth blend — is often a panel or driver limitation (6-bit panels, aggressive power saving). First try a different cable, a different port, and full RGB range in your GPU settings; if it persists on every input, it is the panel.
faqs.q: Why do I see stripes on the gradient slide?

faqs.a: The measurement counts how many frames your browser can render per second, which is capped by the display refresh rate and vsync. A 60 Hz screen will report about 60 Hz even on a fast computer. It is a display measurement, not a GPU benchmark.
faqs.q: Why does my gaming PC report only 60 Hz?

faqs.a: The stuck pixel sometimes unsticks. Display a rapidly flashing red-green-blue pattern on that spot for 10–20 minutes (several free videos do this) or gently massage the area with a soft cloth. If it stays, check your warranty.
faqs.q: Can a stuck pixel be fixed?

monitor-test.formula:
Refresh rate (Hz) = frames rendered / seconds measured
Example: 239 frames counted over 2.0 seconds = 239 / 2.0 = 119.5 Hz, reported as 120 Hz.
howTo: Read your screen's reported resolution, pixel ratio, and color depth on this page.
Optionally press Measure to run a 2-second frame count that estimates the real refresh rate.
Press Start test to go full-screen through 8 slides: black, white, red, green, blue, rainbow gradient, gray ramp, and checkerboard.
On each slide, look closely for stuck or dead pixels, uneven backlight, banding, or ghosting.
Use the arrow keys (or the on-screen buttons) to move between slides, and Esc to exit.
keyFacts: Eight full-screen slides: pure black, white, red, green, blue, rainbow gradient, gray ramp, and a checkerboard — the classic defect-hunting set.
The black slide exposes backlight bleed and clouding; the colored slides expose dead and stuck pixels.
The gray ramp and rainbow gradient reveal color banding and gamma problems at a glance.
The page reports your real resolution, device pixel ratio, color depth, and orientation from browser APIs.
A 2-second animation-frame counter estimates the panel's actual refresh rate in Hz.
Arrow keys switch slides, Esc exits; the test also requests full-screen automatically.
